newsitem.title: USA: French Bourse chief sees Euro starting in 1999.
newsitem.headline: French Bourse chief sees Euro starting in 1999.

text.p: The chairman of SBF-Paris Bourse, the French stock exchange, said on Wednesday he expects the single European currency or Euro to be launched on schedule in January 1999.

"The odds today are greater than ever the EMU (European Monetary Union) will start in 1999," SBF-Paris Bourse chairman Jean-Francois Theodore told a meeting of businessmen and investors at the Harvard Club.
"It's a question of political will," Theodore stressed, in reference to the French and German governments' commitment to the Euro.

"Actually, the irrevocable fixing of the single currency will not really start on Friday, January 1, 1999, but on the following Monday, January 4," further said Theodore of the first trading day in 1999.

The Bourse chairman quipped that January 4, 1999 will be a good date to launch the Euro and Euro-denominated financial contracts since the extended holiday weekend will give traders "time to recover from their New Year hangover."

Theodore noted the Paris Bourse, the fourth largest financial exchange in the world, is the "most advanced" European marketplace equipped to handle Euro-denominated contracts via computerized transactions.
Noting the high rate of savings in France, he said the Euro's creation could allow pension funds to invest in stock instruments denominated in the new currency.
